title: Bernardo Houssay's birth chart
metaDescription: Bernardo Houssay's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 20.4° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 20.4° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 20.4° of Aries is the Sun's exact seat — third decan, 20°–30°, sub-ruled by Jupiter in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 25.0° Pisces, Venus holds 20.8° Taurus, Mars holds 23.7° Aries — in the old shorthand, thought steeped in tone and memory; attraction that grows by reliability; effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury to Neptune is the closest call of the day, a sextile within 1.1°. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, the Sun conjunction Mars at 3.3°, and the Sun square Saturn at 4.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Jupiter makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks five placements here. The Sun in Aries at 20.4° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Pisces at 25.0° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Taurus at 20.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Aries at 23.7° is in domicile; Saturn in Cancer at 16.1° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: water 3, fire 2, earth 2, air 2 across the elements, and cardinal 4, fixed 3, mutable 2 across the modalities. Jupiter and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Scorpio into Sagittarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.5° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
